summary: Restoration provisions in the NDC are framed at EU level: measures in at least 20% of EU land and sea areas each by 2030, peatland and wetland restoration with 51–54 Mt CO2-eq/yr mitigation potential, and reforestation respecting biodiversity plus sustainable forest management with 8–235 Mt CO2-eq/yr potential. For agriculture, improved fertiliser efficiency represents 19 Mt CO2-eq/yr. The mixed land-sector/conservation framework sets a 2030 EU LULUCF balance of 310 Mt CO2 net removals, also expressed as −310 Mt CO2-eq in carbon-sink accounting. Ireland’s own quantified land-sector commitment is −626 Kt CO2eq, combining ecosystem management, emissions and removals; no Irish area, ecosystem allocation, or timeframe is supplied, so it cannot be compared with current forest (4,580 km²; 6.6%), grassland (48,858 km²; 70.1%), wetland (9,210 km²; 13.2%), or agricultural area (4,041 km²; 5.8%). The wider figures are not Ireland-specific hectare or percentage commitments.
